newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-OUB plans major push into unit trusts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-OUB plans major push into unit trusts.

text.p: Singapore's Overseas Union Bank Ltd (OUB) announced a major push into the unit trust business on Friday, targeting the growing heap of surplus cash being generated by Asia's Tiger economies.

OUB President and Chief Executive Officer Peter Seah told Reuters the bank aimed to boost the value of the unit trusts it manages to at least Singapore $200 million (US$139 million) by the turn of the century from around S$40 million now.
Announcing plans to launch the bank's sixth fund, the Global Affluence Fund, Seah said OUB recognised Asian retail investors were getting richer and needed more sophisticated investments.

"With the clearly rising affluence and income levels and a growing need to provide consumers with a choice of investments ranging from fixed deposits to investment products, unit trusts are becoming very important," Seah said in an interview.
"We believe that we will be successful in this new drive and if this new drive brings us over Singapore $100 million by the end of the year, we expect the growth to snowball," he said.
"I would say over the next three years, we aim to at least double that," he added.
Seah said the Singapore unit trust market was fairly small in world terms, but was expected to grow rapidly. Analysts say the total Singapore unit trust market is worth about S$2.9 billion.

"As the public becomes more sophisticated in its use of surplus funds, use of unit trusts will grow," he said. "I am sure before the end of the century we should looking at a market size well in excess of S$5 billion."
"It is just beginning to take off over the last 12-18 months and we think it is a good time and the right time for OUB to come back strongly into the market," Seah said.
"Particularly for those investors who want to participate in the international market, units trusts like a global fund will meet their needs," he said.

OUB is the fourth biggest Singapore bank in terms of interest income but is one of the most profitable and has grown rapidly over the last three years through agressive marketing and expansion out of its domestic Singapore base.
OUB made a net profit of S$310.4 million in 1996 on an interest income of S$1.94 billion.
The bank manages the largest Singapore portfolio of funds for institutions, worth around S$2.5 billion, an OUB official said.
This compares with around S$2.4 billion for the Development Bank of Singapore, S$2.2 billion for Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and S$2.1 billion for United Overseas Bank, analysts said.
"Over the last couple of years we have focused on building up portfolio management, mainly for institutions and high net-worth individuals, particularly beyond regional markets," Seah said.
OUB's Global Affluence Fund aims to invest about 50 percent in health-related companies, 25 percent in tourism, leisure and entertainment firms and the rest in wealth management services.
The fund will invest about 40 percent in the United States, 15 percent in Japan, 25 percent in the rest of Asia and 20 percent in Europe, an OUB statement said.
"We expect the fund to grow at about 10 percent to 15 percent per annum in the medium term," OUB Asset Management executive director Goh Mui Hong told a news conference.
